# Contributing

Thanks for taking the time to improve usbtree.

## Open an issue first

For anything beyond a typo or docs tweak, open an issue before the pull request. It keeps you from building something that is already planned, already rejected, or better solved another way. Link the issue from the pull request.

## Development

Install a stable Rust toolchain, then use the project tasks or Cargo directly:

```sh
cargo test
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
cargo build --release --locked
```

The fake device tree is useful for development without USB hardware:

```sh
cargo run -- --demo
cargo run -- --demo --dump
```

Enable the repo git hooks once per clone — they run a secrets and privacy scan before each commit:

```sh
task hooks          # or: git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

If you have [Task](https://taskfile.dev) installed, `task -l` lists the same common commands (`task test`, `task lint`, `task demo`, `task shots`). CI calls Cargo directly, so Task is optional.

## Pull requests

- Link the issue it resolves.
- Keep changes focused and match the surrounding style. Code is hand-aligned in places, so do not run a blind `cargo fmt` over files you did not touch.
- Add or update tests when changing parsing, tree behavior, device classification, or release/install logic.
- Run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` before opening a pull request.
- Use Conventional Commit-style commit messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `chore:`). Release automation uses them to build the changelog.

## UI changes need before/after screenshots

If a change touches the TUI — layout, colors, columns, key handling, panes — put **before** and **after** screenshots in the pull request description. Same terminal size and same view in both, otherwise the diff is unreadable.

Easiest way to get a reproducible shot, no hardware needed:

```sh
cargo run --release -- --demo
```

Screenshot that, then apply your change and screenshot again.

The published screenshots in `docs/screenshots/` are generated from `tapes/` with [VHS](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) and regenerated by CI, so you do not need to commit them. To render locally (needs `vhs`, `ttyd`, and `ffmpeg`):

```sh
task shots          # or: scripts/shots.sh
```
